mil3.1.5:1.1: Then Venerable Nāgasena went to King Milinda’s residence, and having gone he sat down on the seat that had been prepared.
mil3.1.5:1.2: Then King Milinda, with his own hands, served and satisfied Venerable Nāgasena and his assembly with fine hard and soft foods until they were full. He clothed each mendicant with a pair of cloths, and clothed Venerable Nāgasena with the three robes. Then he said to Venerable Nāgasena—
mil3.1.5:1.3: “Venerable Nāgasena, please sit here with ten mendicants; let the rest depart.”
mil3.1.5:2.1: Then King Milinda, seeing that Venerable Nāgasena had finished his meal and had taken his hand from the bowl, took a low seat and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, King Milinda said to Venerable Nāgasena—
mil3.1.5:2.2: “Venerable Nāgasena, what shall our conversation be about?”
mil3.1.5:2.3: “Great King, we are concerned with the goal; let our conversation be about the goal.”
mil3.1.5:3.2: “Venerable Nāgasena, for what purpose is your going forth, and what is your ultimate goal?”
mil3.1.5:3.4: “The purpose, Great King, is that this suffering might cease, and no other suffering arise.
mil3.1.5:3.5: This, Great King, is the purpose of our going forth; and our ultimate goal is final extinguishment through not grasping.”
mil3.1.5:4.1: “But Venerable Nāgasena, do all go forth for this purpose?”
mil3.1.5:4.2: “No, Great King. Some go forth for this purpose; some go forth to escape a summons by the king, some to escape a summons for a bandit, some because of debt, and some for the sake of a livelihood. But those who go forth rightly go forth for this purpose.”
mil3.1.5:5.1: “But venerable sir, did you go forth for this purpose?”
mil3.1.5:5.2: “Great King, I went forth when I was a boy, and I did not know that I was going forth for the sake of this. But it occurred to me: ‘These ascetics who follow the Sakyan are wise; they will train me.’ Trained by them, I know and see: ‘Going forth is for the sake of this.’”
